extracted_claims.text: The original Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) provided that the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after the Act's entry into force (1 August 2024).
A legislative package known as the 'AI Omnibus' (Digital Omnibus on AI) amended the AI Act to extend the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027.
The AI Omnibus also extended the application date for high-risk AI systems that are products or safety components covered by Annex I (Union harmonisation legislation) to 2 August 2028.

The Commission's original AI Omnibus proposal would have adjusted the high-risk timeline by up to 16 months so that rules start to apply once the Commission confirms needed standards and tools are available, rather than on a fixed calendar date.

The AI Omnibus legislative process proceeded as follows: Commission proposal adopted 19 November 2025; political agreement between Council and Parliament reached 7 May 2026; the regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.

The consolidated official text of the AI Act (version dated 27.07.2026) states that the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market before 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113' (a cross-reference rather than a fixed date), reflecting the post-Omnibus amendment.

Article 113 of the AI Act, as implemented via Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, provides that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (which set out the Annex III high-risk AI system requirements), with the exception of Article 6(5), shall apply from 2 December 2027.

A news blog states that under a 'final text agreed in September 2026' the Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from 2 August 2029 rather than 2 December 2027, due to unreadiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies.

Several commentary and news sources, including ones with no clear publication date or pre-dating the 7 May 2026 political agreement, continue to describe 2 August 2026 as the (current or upcoming) date on which Annex III high-risk obligations become enforceable.
Transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, separate from the Annex III high-risk obligations timeline.
New prohibitions relating to non-consensual intimate deepfakes and child sexual abuse material apply from 2 December 2026, with a related Article 50(2) transition deadline for pre-existing systems.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would take effect, 36 months after the Act's entry into force (high confidence). However, a legislative amendment package known as the "AI Omnibus" entered into force on 27 July 2026 and extended this deadline to **2 December 2027** (high confidence), with a separate, later date of 2 August 2028 for Annex I product-embedded high-risk systems (high confidence). Some commentary sources have not been updated to reflect this change and continue to cite 2026, and one low-confidence, uncorroborated source claims a further postponement to 2029.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) entered into force on 1 August 2024, and originally provided that Annex III high-risk AI system obligations would apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months later (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2026)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
A legislative package, the "Digital Omnibus on AI" (or "AI Omnibus"), amended the AI Act to push back the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([European Commission AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy - AI Omnibus enters force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). The same package further extended the deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded as products or safety components under Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) to **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

The Commission's original Omnibus proposal would have gone further, allowing the timeline to shift by up to 16 months so that rules applied only once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and conformity-assessment tools were available, rather than fixing a calendar date (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Legislative Process
The Omnibus proposal was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The consolidated official EUR-Lex text, dated 27.07.2026, now refers to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" rather than a fixed calendar date, reflecting this amendment (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Article 113, as implemented, specifies that Chapter III Sections 1–3 (the Annex III high-risk requirements), except Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### Related but Distinct Deadlines
Transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, independent of the Annex III timeline (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq)). New prohibitions on non-consensual intimate deepfakes and child sexual abuse material apply from 2 December 2026, with an associated Article 50(2) transition deadline (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources conflict on the operative date. Official post-Omnibus EU guidance consistently cites **2 December 2027**, but a number of undated commentary/news sites still describe 2 August 2026 as the current deadline, indicating they predate or were not updated after the Omnibus amendment ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). A low-confidence (0.12), uncorroborated news blog claims the deadline has shifted further to 2 August 2029, citing an alleged "final text agreed in September 2026" — this is not confirmed by any official EU source and should be treated with significant caution ([ai-act-news-blog.example](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). The European Parliament's topic page, describing a flat 36-month rule, is also inconsistent with both the original and amended dates ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)). Additionally, the AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 page appears not to reflect the Omnibus update, still citing the original fixed date.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether 2 December 2027 is a firm, final date or a "backstop" subject to further adjustment based on Commission confirmation of standards readiness, as originally proposed. The precise breakdown of dates for Annex I product-embedded systems (2027 vs. 2028) is inconsistently reported across sources. The exact legal citation for the Omnibus regulation ("Regulation (EU) 2026/1744") is only referenced in non-official sources and requires verification against the Official Journal.

This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would take effect, 36 months after the Act's entry into force (high confidence). However, a legislative amendment package known as the "AI Omnibus" entered into force on 27 July 2026 and extended this deadline to **2 December 2027** (high confidence), with a separate, later date of 2 August 2028 for Annex I product-embedded high-risk systems (high confidence). Some commentary sources have not been updated to reflect this change and continue to cite 2026, and one low-confidence, uncorroborated source claims a further postponement to 2029.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) entered into force on 1 August 2024, and originally provided that Annex III high-risk AI system obligations would apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months later (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2026)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
A legislative package, the "Digital Omnibus on AI" (or "AI Omnibus"), amended the AI Act to push back the application date for Annex III high-risk obligations to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([European Commission AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy - AI Omnibus enters force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). The same package further extended the deadline for high-risk AI systems embedded as products or safety components under Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) to **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

The Commission's original Omnibus proposal would have gone further, allowing the timeline to shift by up to 16 months so that rules applied only once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and conformity-assessment tools were available, rather than fixing a calendar date (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Legislative Process
The Omnibus proposal was adopted by the Commission on 19 November 2025, political agreement between Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026, and the amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The consolidated official EUR-Lex text, dated 27.07.2026, now refers to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" rather than a fixed calendar date, reflecting this amendment (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). Article 113, as implemented, specifies that Chapter III Sections 1–3 (the Annex III high-risk requirements), except Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)).

### Related but Distinct Deadlines
Transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, independent of the Annex III timeline (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq)). New prohibitions on non-consensual intimate deepfakes and child sexual abuse material apply from 2 December 2026, with an associated Article 50(2) transition deadline (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources conflict on the operative date. Official post-Omnibus EU guidance consistently cites **2 December 2027**, but a number of undated commentary/news sites still describe 2 August 2026 as the current deadline, indicating they predate or were not updated after the Omnibus amendment ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)). A low-confidence (0.12), uncorroborated news blog claims the deadline has shifted further to 2 August 2029, citing an alleged "final text agreed in September 2026" — this is not confirmed by any official EU source and should be treated with significant caution ([ai-act-news-blog.example](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). The European Parliament's topic page, describing a flat 36-month rule, is also inconsistent with both the original and amended dates ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)). Additionally, the AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 page appears not to reflect the Omnibus update, still citing the original fixed date.

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether 2 December 2027 is a firm, final date or a "backstop" subject to further adjustment based on Commission confirmation of standards readiness, as originally proposed. The precise breakdown of dates for Annex I product-embedded systems (2027 vs. 2028) is inconsistently reported across sources. The exact legal citation for the Omnibus regulation ("Regulation (EU) 2026/1744") is only referenced in non-official sources and requires verification against the Official Journal.
